name: Sweet potatoes

default_move.headline: Cut side down. Don't flip it.
steps: cut side down on the pan

why_now: Most of California's sweet potatoes come out of the ground around Merced in September and October. The new crop is on the shelves now — at its cheapest, and not yet tired from months in storage.
how_to_choose: Firm all over, with no soft ends and no sprouts
Medium and even in shape, so they cook at one speed
buy_this_much: 2 lbs. They keep, so they're the thing you cook the week it gets away from you.
weekday_uses: Cut side down beside pork chops
Cubed and roasted into tacos with poblano and pomegranate
In a rice bowl with ground beef
Split open with yogurt, salt, and chile
storage: Somewhere cool and dark, not the fridge — cold turns the center hard and odd-tasting. They keep for weeks.
one_thing_to_learn: Cut side down is the whole trick. The flat face sits on the hot pan and the sugars caramelize into a dark crust while the inside steams in its own skin. Flip it halfway and you lose the crust. Leave it alone.
